books.title: श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता
books.desc: 18 chapters, 700 verses: Sanskrit, Roman transliteration, Gandhi's Hindi meaning and a plain-English meaning.
books.en_note: The English meanings are plain renderings written with Claude directly from the Sanskrit for this reader. They are not a scholarly translation.
books.ocr_note: हिन्दी अर्थ गांधीजी के ‘अनासक्तियोग’ (सस्ता साहित्य मंडल, 1949 संस्करण) से है। यह विकिस्रोत पर स्कैन का OCR पाठ है, जिसकी अभी जाँच (proofreading) नहीं हुई है, इसलिए कहीं-कहीं अक्षर ग़लत हो सकते हैं। हर अर्थ के साथ स्कैन पृष्ठ का लिंक है। The Hindi meaning is unproofread OCR from the Wikisource scan of Gandhi's Anasaktiyoga; some letters may be wrong. Each meaning links to its scan page.

books.title: पराशरस्मृतिः
books.desc: A dharmaśāstra in 12 chapters, all 583 ślokas: Sanskrit, Roman transliteration and a plain-English meaning. Opens one śloka at a time.
about: The Parāśara Smṛti is a dharmaśāstra of twelve chapters, given by the sage Parāśara to his son Vyāsa as the law for the Kali age. The text itself (12.81) says it has 592 ślokas; this edition has 583.

Sanskrit text from Sanskrit Wikisource, used under CC BY-SA 4.0. Verse numbers follow that edition; in chapter 12 the number in brackets is the older numbering. Roman transliteration is generated from the Devanagari.

The English meanings are plain renderings written by Claude directly from the Sanskrit for this reader. They are not a scholarly translation; check a printed edition before relying on a point of law or ritual.
Keys: ← and → turn the page. On a phone, swipe left or right. Type a number such as 3.16 in “Go to” to jump to a śloka.

sa-garuda.title: गरुडपुराणम् — Sanskrit Wikisource
sa-garuda.note: The traditional Sanskrit text is public domain. All three kandas (Achara 240, Preta 49 and Brahma 29 chapter pages) as typed on Wikisource; each chapter links to its page. Verse breaks follow the verse numbers in the source; the Roman transliteration is made by a fixed rule.

sa-markandeya.title: मार्कण्डेयपुराणम् — Sanskrit Wikisource
sa-markandeya.note: The traditional Sanskrit text is public domain. The Wikisource pages hold several adhyayas each; they are split at each closing ‘इति श्रीमार्कण्डेयपुराणे…’ line. 133 of 134 adhyayas are included; adhyaya 37 is not on Wikisource. The Devi Mahatmya (Durga Saptashati) is adhyayas 81–93 of this text. Notes on the Wikisource pages are left out. The Roman transliteration is made by a fixed rule.

sa-vishnu-purana.title: विष्णुपुराणम् — Sanskrit Wikisource
sa-vishnu-purana.note: The traditional Sanskrit text is public domain. All six amshas (126 chapter pages) as typed on Wikisource; each chapter links to its page. Verse breaks follow the verse numbers in the source; the Roman transliteration is made by a fixed rule. No Hindi or English meaning.

claude-en.title: English meanings — plain renderings written with Claude
claude-en.where: Written for this site (stored in sources/en/ in the repository)
claude-en.note: Plain renderings written with Claude directly from the original Sanskrit or Awadhi, one short meaning per verse. They are not a scholarly translation and are not taken from any published translation; check a printed edition before relying on a point. No free public-domain English that lines up verse by verse was found: K. T. Telang's 1882 Gita (Sacred Books of the East, vol. 8) is continuous prose without verse numbers, and is incomplete on Wikisource.

sa-bhagavata.title: श्रीमद्भागवतपुराणम् — Sanskrit Wikisource
sa-bhagavata.note: The traditional Sanskrit text is public domain. Taken from the chapter pages ‘श्रीमद्भागवतपुराणम्/स्कन्धः N/अध्यायः M’; each chapter links to its page. The Roman transliteration is made by a fixed rule. No Hindi meaning is given: the Gita Press Hindi edition is under copyright and is not used.

sa-chanakya.title: चाणक्यनीतिः — Sanskrit Wikisource
sa-chanakya.note: The traditional text is public domain. Verses and numbers are as on the Wikisource page (15 chapters); the Roman transliteration is made by a fixed rule. No openly licensed Hindi meaning was found on Wikisource, so none is given.

sa-vishnu.title: श्रीविष्णुसहस्रनामस्तोत्रम् — Sanskrit Wikisource
sa-vishnu.note: The traditional text is public domain. The Wikisource page notes that it was converted from the ITRANS version at sanskritdocuments.org. Verses, headings and numbers are as on that page; the Roman transliteration is made by a fixed rule.

sa-lalita.title: श्री ललितासहस्रनामस्तोत्रम् — Sanskrit Wikisource
sa-lalita.note: The traditional text (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) is public domain. This is the typed text on Wikisource, used as it stands, so a few typing errors may remain. The source does not number the verses.

sa-shiva.title: शिवसहस्रनामस्तोत्रम् — बृहत्स्तोत्ररत्नाकरः (प्रथमः भागः), 1953
sa-shiva.where: Sanskrit Wikisource transcription of the scanned book, pages validated by Wikisource volunteers
sa-shiva.licence: Traditional text, public domain; Wikisource transcription CC BY-SA 4.0
sa-shiva.note: Mahābhārata, Anuśāsana Parva, chapter 17, as printed in the Bṛhat Stotra Ratnākara. All 182 ślokas; the opening dhyāna verse and speaker lines are as in the book.

premchand.title: मानसरोवर, भाग १ और २ — प्रेमचंद
premchand.where: Hindi Wikisource transcriptions of the Mansarovar volumes (Saraswati Press, Banaras)
premchand.licence: Public domain in India (Premchand died in 1936); Wikisource transcription CC BY-SA 4.0
premchand.note: Premchand's own Hindi stories, not translations. A story is included only when every scan page it uses is marked proofread or validated on Wikisource; 8 stories were left out because some of their pages are not yet proofread (घर जमाई, गुल्ली-डण्डा, ठाकुर का कुआँ, लांछन, शिकार, रियासत का दीवान, बासी भात में खुदा का साझा, शूद्रा). Page numbers and running headers are removed; the words are as on Wikisource. Each story links to its Wikisource page.

sa-parashara.title: पराशरस्मृतिः — संस्कृत पाठ (Sanskrit text)
sa-parashara.where: Sanskrit Wikisource (sa.wikisource.org), via the Parāśara Smṛti reader (github.com/tiwari91/parashara-smriti, commit 7636992)

Only scan pages that Wikisource volunteers have proofread are used; unproofread pages are shown as gaps with a link to the scan. The Roman transliteration is made by a fixed rule.

sa-gita.note: Verse text only, taken from the 18 chapter pages. The Roman transliteration is made from it by a fixed rule (tools/iast.py).

anasakti.title: अनासक्तियोग — मोहनदास करमचंद गांधी (Hindi meaning)
anasakti.where: Hindi Wikisource scan of the 1949 (6th) edition, Sasta Sahitya Mandal, New Delhi; first published 1929–30. Scan from the Digital Library of India.
anasakti.licence: Public domain in India (PD-India); text pages on Wikisource are CC BY-SA 4.0
anasakti.note: Gandhi died in 1948, so his writings are public domain in India (life + 60 years). The Hindi version is an unnamed rendering of Gandhi's Gujarati, published by Sasta Sahitya Mandal. The text here is the unproofread OCR on Wikisource, used as it stands: only running headers, page numbers, scan noise and Gandhi's notes (टिप्पणी) are left out. Verses 6.42–6.45 (scan page blank), 8.20 and 18.73–18.74 (OCR too damaged) have no meaning.
